analysis.investment_thesis: Landmark Global is a micro-cap (INR 51.8 Cr) immigration consultancy with an optically low P/E of 5.25 but a trivial ROE of 0.21%, suggesting either collapsed earnings or an accounting artifact. Without a multi-year earnings record, dividend history, or balance-sheet visibility, this fails every Graham quantitative filter.
key_strengths: P/E of 5.25 is superficially below my <15 threshold
Promoter holding of 72.44% signals skin in the game
Asset-light consultancy model requires limited capex
key_risks: ROE of 0.21% is essentially zero — no real earning power
Micro-cap (INR 51.8 Cr) with near-zero institutional ownership (0% FII, 3.37% DII)
Recent listing (BSE code 544341) means no multi-year audited track record
red_flags: ROE of 0.21% contradicts the low P/E — earnings quality is suspect
No visible dividend history or balance-sheet disclosure (current ratio, D/E, book value unknown)
Recent IPO — the seller always knows more than the buyer
Tiny float and virtually no institutional validation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The headline P/E of 5.25 would normally catch my eye, but a 0.21% ROE tells the real story: this company is earning roughly nothing on its equity base. Either the denominator (equity) is inflated by recent IPO proceeds not yet deployed, or earnings are a one-off rounding. Either way, there is no "proven earning power" here — the cornerstone of intrinsic value in my framework. At a INR 51.8 Cr market cap with essentially no institutional following, Mr. Market is not offering a bargain; he is offering a lottery ticket.

I have no visibility into the current ratio, debt-to-equity, interest coverage, book value, or dividend record — all non-negotiable inputs for a Graham-style valuation. An immigration consultancy is a cyclical, regulation-sensitive, people-dependent service business with negligible tangible assets to underwrite a margin of safety. Combined with the IPO-vintage listing and a 72%+ promoter holding that leaves a thin public float, this is a speculation, not an investment. Avoid.
